claims.text: Acute primary: ⍉antifungal unless ⍉spont improvement after 1 mo or immunocompromised - then PO itraconazole TID for 3 days, then BID for 6 to 12 wks
claims.quote: Acute primary histoplasmosis requires no antifungal therapy unless there is no spontaneous improvement after 1 month or unless the patient is immunocompromised (1, 3), in which case treatment is with oral itraconazole 3 times a day for 3 days, then 2 times a day for 6 to 12 weeks.

claims.text: Chronic cavitary: PO itraconazole for 12 to 24 mo
claims.quote: For chronic cavitary histoplasmosis, oral itraconazole is given for 12 to 24 months.

claims.text: Severe disseminated: IV liposomal amphotericin B Q1x day for 2 wks or until clinically stable = tx of choice;
claims.quote: For severe disseminated histoplasmosis, IV liposomal amphotericin B once a day for 2 weeks or until the patient is clinically stable is the treatment of choice.

claims.text: then PO itraconazole TID for 3 days, then BID for 12 mo after afebrile & off ventilatory & BP support
claims.quote: Patients can then be switched to oral itraconazole 3 times a day for 3 days, then 2 times a day continued for 12 months after they become afebrile and require no ventilatory or blood pressure support.
Posaconazole and isavuconazonium are active against H. capsulatum and may be effective in the treatment of patients with histoplasmosis.

claims.text: Fluconazole & voriconazole may be less effective
claims.quote: Fluconazole and voriconazole may be less effective (1).
